q: Plants use carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll and light to compose _____ and oxygen.
e: Plants use carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll and light to compose glucose and oxygen. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Cellulose is different: cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid.

q: Photosynthesis takes place in the _____ of the green parts of plants but mainly in the leaves.
e: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of the green parts of plants but mainly in the leaves. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Mitochondria is different: mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production.

q: For photosynthesis efficiency, leaves need to have a large surface area to absorb light, much chlorophyll to catch the light, and veins including _____ to supply water.
e: For photosynthesis efficiency, leaves need to have a large surface area to absorb light, much chlorophyll to catch the light, and veins including xylem and phloem to supply water. Phloem carries sugars away from the leaf to the rest of the plant. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Palisade and spongy mesophyll is not xylem and phloem.

q: Most leaves are thin, flat structures supported by _____ which support the leaf blade to be angled to receive the maximum amount of sunlight.
e: Most leaves are thin, flat structures supported by petiole which support the leaf blade to be angled to receive the maximum amount of sunlight. The petiole holds the leaf blade at an angle that catches light. Midrib is not petiole.

q: In many plants, there is a thin waxy layer called the _____ over the epidermis.
e: In many plants, there is a thin waxy layer called the cuticle over the epidermis. The waxy cuticle cuts unwanted water loss from the leaf surface. Guard cell is not cuticle.

q: In most dicotyledonous plants, the stomata occur only in the _____.
e: In most dicotyledonous plants, the stomata occur only in the lower epidermis. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out. Mesophyll is different: mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue between the upper and lower epidermis.

q: In monocotyledonous plants, the stomata are _____ distributed on both surfaces of the leaf.
e: In monocotyledonous plants, the stomata are equally distributed on both surfaces of the leaf. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out. Randomly is not equally.

q: The tissue between the upper and lower epidermis is called _____.
e: The tissue between the upper and lower epidermis is called mesophyll. Cuticle is different: the waxy cuticle cuts unwanted water loss from the leaf surface.

q: The palisade mesophyll cells are usually long and contain many _____.
e: The palisade mesophyll cells are usually long and contain many chloroplasts. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue between the upper and lower epidermis. Sieve plates is not chloroplasts.

q: The spongy mesophyll cells vary in shape and are loosely arranged with many _____ between them.
e: The spongy mesophyll cells vary in shape and are loosely arranged with many air spaces between them. Leaf air spaces connect stomata to mesophyll so gases can diffuse. Mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue between the upper and lower epidermis. Xylem vessels is not air spaces.

q: The major vein of the leaf is called the _____ continuation of petiole.
e: The major vein of the leaf is called the midrib continuation of petiole. The petiole holds the leaf blade at an angle that catches light. Cuticle is different: the waxy cuticle cuts unwanted water loss from the leaf surface.

q: In xylem, vessels are cylindrical, hollow and _____ cells.
e: In xylem, vessels are cylindrical, hollow and thick walled cells. Xylem brings water and minerals up to the photosynthetic cells. Perforated is not thick walled.

q: The phloem consists of sieve tubes which are elongated cells and the transverse walls of sieve tubes are perforated _____.
e: The phloem consists of sieve tubes which are elongated cells and the transverse walls of sieve tubes are perforated sieve plates. Phloem carries sugars away from the leaf to the rest of the plant. Guard cells is different: guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: The epidermal cells are thin to allow light to pass through and _____ are absent.
e: The epidermal cells are thin to allow light to pass through and Chloroplasts are absent. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Ribosomes is different: ribosomes assemble proteins; they are not the site of photosynthesis.

q: The _____ helps to keep the leaf's shape and to reduce water loss, acting as a barrier to disease organisms.
e: The Upper epidermis helps to keep the leaf's shape and to reduce water loss, acting as a barrier to disease organisms. Spongy mesophyll is not Upper epidermis.

q: The _____ allows diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen in and out of mesophyll cells.
e: The Spongy mesophyll allows diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen in and out of mesophyll cells. Mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue between the upper and lower epidermis. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Xylem is different: xylem brings water and minerals up to the photosynthetic cells.

q: Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed by _____ to leaves.
e: Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed by roots to leaves. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low. Xylem brings water and minerals up to the photosynthetic cells. Flowers is not roots.

q: Phloem transports photosynthetic products to _____ of the plant.
e: Phloem transports photosynthetic products to other parts of the plant. Phloem carries sugars away from the leaf to the rest of the plant. The roots only is not other parts.

q: The stoma is the site of _____ into and out of the leaf.
e: The stoma is the site of gaseous exchange into and out of the leaf. Gaseous exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Water absorption is not gaseous exchange.

q: Chloroplast is a membrane bound organelle containing chlorophyll a, b and _____.
e: Chloroplast is a membrane bound organelle containing chlorophyll a, b and other pigments. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy. Ribosomes only is not other pigments.

q: Chloroplasts found in higher plants are generally _____ shaped.
e: Chloroplasts found in higher plants are generally biconvex shaped. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Spherical is not biconvex.

q: The outer membrane of chloroplast is a semi-porous membrane and is permeable to _____ which diffuse easily.
e: The outer membrane of chloroplast is a semi-porous membrane and is permeable to small molecules and ions which diffuse easily. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Starch granules is not small molecules and ions.

q: The intermembrane space is a thin space about _____ and it lies between the outer and the inner membranes of the chloroplast.
e: The intermembrane space is a thin space about 10-20 nm and it lies between the outer and the inner membranes of the chloroplast. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. 1-2 nm is not 10-20 nm.

q: The inner membrane of the chloroplast forms a border to the _____ and regulates passage of materials.
e: The inner membrane of the chloroplast forms a border to the stroma and regulates passage of materials. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. Stroma is the chloroplast fluid around the thylakoids. Thylakoid is different: thylakoid membranes hold chlorophyll and run the light-dependent reactions.

q: The _____ is the site for the dark reaction of photosynthesis.
e: The stroma is the site for the dark reaction of photosynthesis. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process. Thylakoid membrane is not stroma.

q: The thylakoids are suspended in the stroma and are membranous sacs which are arranged in stacks known as _____.
e: The thylakoids are suspended in the stroma and are membranous sacs which are arranged in stacks known as grana. Grana are stacks of thylakoids inside a chloroplast. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. Stroma lamellae is not grana.

q: Each granum contains around _____ thylakoids.
e: Each granum contains around 10-20 thylakoids. 50-100 is not 10-20.

q: The thylakoid membrane is the site for the _____ of photosynthesis.
e: The thylakoid membrane is the site for the light reactions of photosynthesis. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. Calvin cycle is different: the Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugar in the stroma.

q: Chlorophyll reflects mostly the _____ portion of light.
e: Chlorophyll reflects mostly the green portion of light. Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy.

q: The wavelengths of light almost totally absorbed by chlorophyll are blue (480 nm) and _____.
e: The wavelengths of light almost totally absorbed by chlorophyll are blue (480 nm) and red (700 nm). Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy. Yellow (600 nm) is not red (700 nm).

q: Photosynthesis comprises of two phases: the light reaction and the _____.
e: Photosynthesis comprises of two phases: the light reaction and the dark reaction. The dark reaction, or Calvin cycle, uses ATP and NADPH to make sugar and does not need light directly. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH. Krebs cycle is not dark reaction.

q: The light reaction takes place on the _____ of chloroplast.
e: The light reaction takes place on the thylakoid membrane of chloroplast. Thylakoid membranes hold chlorophyll and run the light-dependent reactions. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH. Outer membrane is not thylakoid membrane.

q: The dark reaction takes place in the _____ of the chloroplast.
e: The dark reaction takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. Stroma is the chloroplast fluid around the thylakoids. Intermembrane space is not stroma.

q: The light reaction is a light-dependent process which includes light absorption, photolysis and release of oxygen and formation of chemical compounds: ATP and _____.
e: The light reaction is a light-dependent process which includes light absorption, photolysis and release of oxygen and formation of chemical compounds: ATP and NADPH. NADPH is the reduced coenzyme that carries high-energy electrons to the Calvin cycle. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH. Glucose is different: glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: The dark reaction is also called _____.
e: The dark reaction is also called Calvin cycle. The Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugar in the stroma. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process. Krebs cycle is not Calvin cycle.

q: The dark reaction is a light-independent process in which sugar molecules are formed by using carbon dioxide with the help of ATP and _____ produced from the light reaction.
e: The dark reaction is a light-independent process in which sugar molecules are formed by using carbon dioxide with the help of ATP and NADPH produced from the light reaction. NADPH is the reduced coenzyme that carries high-energy electrons to the Calvin cycle. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: In the light reaction, the water molecules split into hydrogen and _____.
e: In the light reaction, the water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Splitting water in the light reactions is the source of photosynthetic oxygen. Carbon dioxide is different: carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: In the dark reaction, glucose molecules are formed using _____.
e: In the dark reaction, glucose molecules are formed using CO2. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process. The dark reaction, or Calvin cycle, uses ATP and NADPH to make sugar and does not need light directly. O2 is not CO2.

q: Photolysis occurs in the light reaction and _____ in the dark reaction.
e: Photolysis occurs in the light reaction and does not occur in the dark reaction. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process. Occurs slowly is not does not occur.

q: As the light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases until it reaches a _____.
e: As the light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases until it reaches a maximum rate. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Minimum rate is not maximum rate.

q: Under bright light, the rate of photosynthesis increases with a rise in temperature up to a maximum temperature of around _____.
e: Under bright light, the rate of photosynthesis increases with a rise in temperature up to a maximum temperature of around 40°C. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. 60°C is not 40°C.

q: Beyond the maximum temperature, the rate of photosynthesis drops _____.
e: Beyond the maximum temperature, the rate of photosynthesis drops rapidly. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Gradually is not rapidly.

q: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is about _____.
e: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is about 0.04%. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. 4.0% is not 0.04%.

q: There are four requirements of photosynthesis, namely chlorophyll, light, carbon dioxide and _____.
e: There are four requirements of photosynthesis, namely chlorophyll, light, carbon dioxide and water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: In each investigation for requirements of photosynthesis, the plants must first be _____.
e: In each investigation for requirements of photosynthesis, the plants must first be destarched. A destarched leaf has used up its starch, so new starch after light is evidence of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Fertilized is not destarched.

q: The leaves are destarched by placing this plant in the dark for _____.
e: The leaves are destarched by placing this plant in the dark for 2-3 days. A destarched leaf has used up its starch, so new starch after light is evidence of photosynthesis. 2-3 hours is not 2-3 days.

q: Variegated leaves which have chlorophyll as green patches can be found in plants like Coleus, spiderwort and _____.
e: Variegated leaves which have chlorophyll as green patches can be found in plants like Coleus, spiderwort and croton. Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy. Sunflower is not croton.

q: Only the green patches previously will turn _____ with iodine solution.
e: Only the green patches previously will turn blue-black with iodine solution. Starch plus iodine gives a blue-black colour. Iodine solution turns blue-black with starch. Yellow is not blue-black.

q: In the investigation to show that light is essential, a portion of green leaf is sandwiched between two pieces of black paper or black tape or _____.
e: In the investigation to show that light is essential, a portion of green leaf is sandwiched between two pieces of black paper or black tape or aluminium foil. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Plastic wrap is not aluminium foil.

q: In the investigation for carbon dioxide, NaHCO3 is put inside set-up A for producing carbon dioxide and _____ inside set-up B to absorb carbon dioxide.
e: In the investigation for carbon dioxide, NaHCO3 is put inside set-up A for producing carbon dioxide and NaOH inside set-up B to absorb carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. H2SO4 is not NaOH.

q: Leaf from the plant in which NaOH has been placed will stain _____.
e: Leaf from the plant in which NaOH has been placed will stain brown. Brown adipose tissue can generate heat by uncoupled respiration. Blue-black is different: starch plus iodine gives a blue-black colour.

q: Respiration involves a number of chemical reactions that break down nutrient molecules, such as glucose, in living cells to release _____.
e: Respiration involves a number of chemical reactions that break down nutrient molecules, such as glucose, in living cells to release energy. Living systems need a continual energy input to keep organised. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: There are two types of respiration: aerobic respiration and _____ respiration.
e: There are two types of respiration: aerobic respiration and anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Photosynthetic is not anaerobic.

q: In prokaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the _____.
e: In prokaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: In eukaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the _____ of cells.
e: In eukaryotic organisms, aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria of cells. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Chloroplasts is different: chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: Anaerobic respiration takes place in the _____ of plant cells, animal cells and some microorganisms.
e: Anaerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm of plant cells, animal cells and some microorganisms. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: A mitochondrion has two membranes: an outer membrane and an _____.
e: A mitochondrion has two membranes: an outer membrane and an inner membrane. Membranes are phospholipid bilayers that control transport and keep compartments. The inner mitochondrial membrane holds the electron-transport chain. Outer wall is not inner membrane.

q: Each membrane of a mitochondrion is made up of _____.
e: Each membrane of a mitochondrion is made up of phospholipid bilayer. Phospholipids form a bilayer with hydrophilic heads out and hydrophobic tails in. The plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins. Protein only is not phospholipid bilayer.

q: The inner membrane of a mitochondrion has many folds called _____.
e: The inner membrane of a mitochondrion has many folds called cristae. Cristae are inner-membrane folds that increase the surface for electron transport. The inner mitochondrial membrane holds the electron-transport chain. Stroma is different: the stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar.

q: An increased surface area creates more space for more reactions to occur and increases the mitochondria's _____.
e: An increased surface area creates more space for more reactions to occur and increases the mitochondria's output. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Size is not output.

q: The space between the outer and inner membranes is called the _____.
e: The space between the outer and inner membranes is called the inter-membrane space. Membranes are phospholipid bilayers that control transport and keep compartments. The inner mitochondrial membrane holds the electron-transport chain. Stroma is different: the stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar.

q: The space inside the inner membrane is called the _____.
e: The space inside the inner membrane is called the matrix. The inner mitochondrial membrane holds the electron-transport chain. Cristae is different: cristae are inner-membrane folds that increase the surface for electron transport.

q: Mitochondria can store _____, which maintains homeostasis of calcium levels in the cell.
e: Mitochondria can store calcium, which maintains homeostasis of calcium levels in the cell. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits. Potassium is not calcium.

q: Mitochondria have roles in apoptosis, cell signaling, and _____ (heat production).
e: Mitochondria have roles in apoptosis, cell signaling, and thermogenesis (heat production). Thermogenesis is heat production, including from brown fat or shivering. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. Glycolysis is different: glycolysis splits glucose in the cytoplasm and yields a little ATP without oxygen.

q: In aerobic respiration, glucose is broken down to release energy in the presence of oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and _____.
e: In aerobic respiration, glucose is broken down to release energy in the presence of oxygen, forming carbon dioxide and water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Ethanol is different: yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration releases _____ of energy.
e: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration releases 2830 kJ of energy. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and yields far more ATP than anaerobic pathways. 36 kJ is not 2830 kJ.

q: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration produces _____ ATP.
e: The balanced chemical equation for aerobic respiration produces 36-38 ATP. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and yields far more ATP than anaerobic pathways. 2 is not 36-38.

q: Insect flight muscle has numerous mitochondria located between the _____.
e: Insect flight muscle has numerous mitochondria located between the muscle fibre. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. Skin cells is not muscle fibre.

q: Liver cells have a high metabolism and have _____ mitochondria.
e: Liver cells have a high metabolism and have many mitochondria. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. The liver stores glycogen, makes bile, and handles many blood chemicals. Liver cells have a high metabolism and have mitochondria.

q: The epithelial cells of the small intestine absorb glucose and other molecules by active transport, so have _____ numbers of mitochondria.
e: The epithelial cells of the small intestine absorb glucose and other molecules by active transport, so have large numbers of mitochondria. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production. The epithelial cells of the small intestine absorb glucose and other molecules by active transport, so have numbers of mitochondria.

q: In the experiment to demonstrate CO2 release in plants, a small glass tube containing 4 ml of _____ solution is hung into the conical flask.
e: In the experiment to demonstrate CO2 release in plants, a small glass tube containing 4 ml of potassium hydroxide solution is hung into the conical flask. Sodium hydroxide is not potassium hydroxide.

q: In the plant respiration experiment, the level of water rises in the glass tube because the CO2 gas is absorbed by _____ solution.
e: In the plant respiration experiment, the level of water rises in the glass tube because the CO2 gas is absorbed by KOH solution. KOH or soda-lime absorbs carbon dioxide in photosynthesis experiments. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. NaHCO3 is not KOH.

q: In the animal respiration experiment, air is drawn through the thistle funnel of _____ which absorbs all the atmospheric carbon dioxide.
e: In the animal respiration experiment, air is drawn through the thistle funnel of soda-lime which absorbs all the atmospheric carbon dioxide. Soda-lime absorbs carbon dioxide, so it can be used to test if photosynthesis needs CO2. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Water is different: water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.

q: In the animal respiration experiment, if the animal is producing carbon dioxide, the lime water in bottle B will turn _____.
e: In the animal respiration experiment, if the animal is producing carbon dioxide, the lime water in bottle B will turn milky. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Clear is not milky.

q: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose into energy in the _____ of oxygen.
e: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose into energy in the absence of oxygen. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. Excess is not absence.

q: Microorganisms such as yeast respire anaerobically by converting glucose into ethanol and _____.
e: Microorganisms such as yeast respire anaerobically by converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi. Lactic acid is different: lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short.

q: The process of yeast converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide is also termed as _____.
e: The process of yeast converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide is also termed as alcohol fermentation. Fermentation is microbial chemical change of organic material, with or without oxygen in modern use. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Lactic acid fermentation is not alcohol fermentation.

q: The anaerobic respiration of glucose in yeast releases _____ of energy.
e: The anaerobic respiration of glucose in yeast releases 118 kJ of energy. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. 36 kJ is not 118 kJ.

q: The anaerobic respiration of glucose in yeast produces _____ ATP.
e: The anaerobic respiration of glucose in yeast produces 2 ATP. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. 38 is not 2.

q: During strenuous exercise, muscle tissue respires anaerobically to release energy, and glucose is broken down to _____ instead of carbon dioxide and water.
e: During strenuous exercise, muscle tissue respires anaerobically to release energy, and glucose is broken down to lactic acid instead of carbon dioxide and water. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Muscles make lactic acid when they respire anaerobically. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: During vigorous exercise, lactic acid builds up in the muscles and blood, and causes the _____.
e: During vigorous exercise, lactic acid builds up in the muscles and blood, and causes the oxygen debt. Oxygen debt is the extra oxygen needed after anaerobic work to clear lactate. Oxygen debt is repaid after anaerobic muscle work. Photosynthesis is different: photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: The oxygen debt is removed during recovery by _____ respiration of lactic acid in the liver.
e: The oxygen debt is removed during recovery by aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and yields far more ATP than anaerobic pathways. Oxygen debt is repaid after anaerobic muscle work. Anaerobic is different: anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP.

q: After exercise the heart continues to beat at a fast rate in order to transport lactic acid in the blood from the muscles to the _____.
e: After exercise the heart continues to beat at a fast rate in order to transport lactic acid in the blood from the muscles to the liver. The liver stores glycogen, makes bile, and handles many blood chemicals. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short.

q: Lactic acid must be broken down in the liver by breathing faster and deeper in order to supply more _____.
e: Lactic acid must be broken down in the liver by breathing faster and deeper in order to supply more oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Carbon dioxide is different: carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: In the anaerobic respiration experiment with germinating seeds, the level of mercury in the test tube falls because of the collection of _____.
e: In the anaerobic respiration experiment with germinating seeds, the level of mercury in the test tube falls because of the collection of carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: In the anaerobic respiration experiment, killed seeds are used as a _____.
e: In the anaerobic respiration experiment, killed seeds are used as a control. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. Catalyst is different: a catalyst speeds a reaction and is not consumed by it.

q: ATP is a nucleotide that consists of three main structures: the nitrogenous base adenine, the pentose sugar ribose, and a chain of _____.
e: ATP is a nucleotide that consists of three main structures: the nitrogenous base adenine, the pentose sugar ribose, and a chain of three phosphate groups. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base.

q: The ATP molecule is formed by bounding adenosine diphosphate to a phosphate group in _____ and absorbs energy released from glucose.
e: The ATP molecule is formed by bounding adenosine diphosphate to a phosphate group in cytoplasm and absorbs energy released from glucose. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus. ATP holds usable energy in its phosphate bonds. Cell wall is not cytoplasm.

q: The energy released from ATP can be used for cell division and growth, synthesis of proteins, fats, vitamins, conduction of nerve impulses, maintenance of constant body temperature, and _____.
e: The energy released from ATP can be used for cell division and growth, synthesis of proteins, fats, vitamins, conduction of nerve impulses, maintenance of constant body temperature, and active transport. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient. ATP holds usable energy in its phosphate bonds. Passive transport is not active transport.

q: In the experiment to demonstrate the release of energy in germinating seeds, the soaked pea seeds are rinsed with 1% formalin for 5 minutes to kill the _____ on the surface.
e: In the experiment to demonstrate the release of energy in germinating seeds, the soaked pea seeds are rinsed with 1% formalin for 5 minutes to kill the bacteria or fungi on the surface. Plant cells is not bacteria or fungi.

q: In the energy release experiment, the temperature in the flask with the living seedlings will be _____ than in the control.
e: In the energy release experiment, the temperature in the flask with the living seedlings will be higher than in the control. Higher is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The products of one process (photosynthesis or respiration) are the _____ of the other.
e: The products of one process (photosynthesis or respiration) are the reactants of the other. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Waste products is not reactants.

q: Photosynthesis makes the glucose that is used in cellular respiration to make _____.
e: Photosynthesis makes the glucose that is used in cellular respiration to make ATP. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: While water is broken down to form oxygen during photosynthesis, in cellular respiration oxygen is combined with hydrogen to form _____.
e: While water is broken down to form oxygen during photosynthesis, in cellular respiration oxygen is combined with hydrogen to form water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Carbon dioxide is different: carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: Cellular respiration works best in the presence of _____.
e: Cellular respiration works best in the presence of oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Carbon dioxide is different: carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: Without oxygen, much less _____ would be produced during cellular respiration.
e: Without oxygen, much less ATP would be produced during cellular respiration. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Glucose is different: glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: The exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis and cellular respiration worldwide helps to keep atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide at _____ levels.
e: The exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis and cellular respiration worldwide helps to keep atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide at stable levels. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Zero is not stable.

q: Photosynthesis occurs only in plants and _____.
e: Photosynthesis occurs only in plants and cyanobacteria. Some cyanobacteria can photosynthesize and also fix nitrogen. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Fungi is not cyanobacteria.

q: Respiration occurs in _____ organisms.
e: Respiration occurs in all living organisms. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Animal only is not all living.

q: Photosynthesis takes place in the presence of light, while respiration takes place _____.
e: Photosynthesis takes place in the presence of light, while respiration takes place throughout the day. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Only at night is not throughout the day.

q: In photosynthesis, light energy is fixed in the form of chemical energy and stored in _____.
e: In photosynthesis, light energy is fixed in the form of chemical energy and stored in carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Proteins is different: proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: In respiration, chemical energy stored in carbohydrates burns to release _____.
e: In respiration, chemical energy stored in carbohydrates burns to release energy. Living systems need a continual energy input to keep organised. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure. Light is different: light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis.
